originality.rationale: The closest fully inspected published graphical-discotope ellipsoid theorems require regularity of the whole graph or biregular bipartiteness; this graph cone has apex degree n and rim degree \(d+1<n\), and it contains triangles. Its outer Euclidean sphere and exact \(2^{n+1}\)-point graph-independent contact constellation, plus an inverse regularity criterion, are not implied by those cited statements. The original discotope papers analyze algebraic boundary, exposed faces, and fiber operations rather than this Euclidean outer metric. The available prior complete-split edge pattern and segment-sum cone law do not dominate arbitrary regular rim disk sums. The checked published-finding corpus searches revealed no exact matching statement or stronger covering theorem. Historical priority can still be affected by unindexed equivalent zonoid results.
residual_risks: Indexed search and selected full-text checks cannot rule out an unindexed exact Euclidean norm identity for graph-cone zonoids under other terminology.
The converse requires a strictly interior maximizing squared-coordinate vector; it makes no assertion for boundary optima of irregular graphs.

value.rationale: The exact Euclidean outer-sphere contacts of a nonregular family of convex zonoids are invariant under replacing the rim with any other d-regular graph on the same n vertices, even when the graphs are nonisomorphic and their edge structure differs. The result classifies all \(2^{n+1}\) contact points and \(2^n\) diametral pairs, and gives a reverse degree-regularity criterion. Global convex-body extrema and full contact sets are natural invariants; the graph-independent contact constellation is a structural fact not implied by the known regular-graph or bipartite formulas.
